declared_parity.parity_note: TWO declared residuals, measured separately, both structural to the backend rather than to this scene. (1) THE ROBOT'S 18 MESHES ARE SHADED PER PIXEL AND MuJoCo SHADES THEM PER VERTEX. MuJoCo draws meshes as triangles with Gouraud interpolation of vertex colours; an analytic per-pixel Blinn-Phong evaluation lands within a level or two of it and not on it. The robot is 8.9% of the frame and carries essentially all of the interior residual -- 0.8% of interior pixels, at an interior mean of 0.009/255, i.e. the disagreement is one level where it exists at all. This is the same limit the OGBench port records and refuted three ways (Gouraud over MuJoCo's own tessellation scored WORSE than plain per-pixel there), and it bites here because a Fetch mover is 9% of the frame rather than 20 pixels. (2) THE TRANSLUCENT MOCAP MARKERS ARE NOT DRAWN. robot0:mocap carries a 1 cm cube at alpha 0.7 and three 2 m crosshair bars at alpha 0.1; mujoco_warp's shader reads only color[0..2] and packs a constant 255, so it has no alpha path at all and would paint them opaque saturated green. Measured against a reference with them hidden: they are 1.2-1.5% of ALL pixels (mean 0.32/255) and 0.000002 of INTERIOR pixels -- a translucent bar over a flat surface leaves no flat 3x3 neighbourhood, so none of it reaches the interior metric. That is also why mocap is not in the state: it reaches no other pixel. What is NOT in these numbers, because it was found and fixed: the float->uint8 quantisation rule (mujoco_warp truncates, GL rounds), worth interior 0.791 -> 0.9988 on its own. The static 91% of the frame -- floor, table, skybox -- is exact by construction, because it is baked through MuJoCo itself.

declared_parity.parity_note: TWO declared residuals, measured separately, both structural to the backend rather than to this scene. (1) THE ROBOT'S 18 MESHES ARE SHADED PER PIXEL AND MuJoCo SHADES THEM PER VERTEX. MuJoCo draws meshes as triangles with Gouraud interpolation of vertex colours; an analytic per-pixel Blinn-Phong evaluation lands within a level or two of it and not on it. The robot is 8.9% of the frame and carries essentially all of the interior residual -- 0.8% of interior pixels, at an interior mean of 0.009/255, i.e. the disagreement is one level where it exists at all. This is the same limit the OGBench port records and refuted three ways (Gouraud over MuJoCo's own tessellation scored WORSE than plain per-pixel there), and it bites here because a Fetch mover is 9% of the frame rather than 20 pixels. (2) THE TRANSLUCENT MOCAP MARKERS ARE NOT DRAWN. robot0:mocap carries a 1 cm cube at alpha 0.7 and three 2 m crosshair bars at alpha 0.1; mujoco_warp's shader reads only color[0..2] and packs a constant 255, so it has no alpha path at all and would paint them opaque saturated green. Measured against a reference with them hidden: they are 1.2-1.5% of ALL pixels (mean 0.32/255) and 0.000002 of INTERIOR pixels -- a translucent bar over a flat surface leaves no flat 3x3 neighbourhood, so none of it reaches the interior metric. That is also why mocap is not in the state: it reaches no other pixel. What is NOT in these numbers, because it was found and fixed: the float->uint8 quantisation rule (mujoco_warp truncates, GL rounds), worth interior 0.791 -> 0.9988 on its own. The static 91% of the frame -- floor, table, skybox -- is exact by construction, because it is baked through MuJoCo itself.
